Up here in Alaska, we have a Governor and Lieutenant Governor that were running in the republican and democrat (respectively) primary election last year. They both left their party's primaries and formed what they called the unity ticket. The fact that they were willing to cooperate and "work across the isle" really spoke to a lot of people that were tired of rhetoric and the parties not working together. They handily beat the incumbent Governor, and they have since earned the respect and trust of a lot of people.

While the US at large obviously operates MUCH differently than Alaska, and I think this idea will likely not go over well with most people in this crowd; I would love to see Rand and Bernie form a unity ticket of their own. I really wouldn't care who was running for the top position. If they were elected and able to work together to form a balanced cabinet and administration (even if skewed towards the ideology of one or the other), I sincerely believe that it would set the tone of cooperation that would hopefully carry over into the legislative body.

Of course a lot of parts of their ideologies are vastly different from one another (polar opposites in some regards), but there is overlap in many other areas, such as foreign intervention, privacy issues, freedom of the internet, freedom of speech. There are also areas where there is at least some overlap and where there can be compromise.

Obviously it is easy to wish this could happen and that they would actually compromise on issues to make a balanced approach to governance. The reality of course is that this will probably never happen, and even if it did it might prove to be a failed experiment. Nonetheless, I for one would love to see them try. I think the country would benefit from some of the policies of both camps, and if nothing else I would take immense pleasure watching the "established" parties shit themselves as it all unfolds.

Thanks for indulging this hypothetical. I would be interested in what others think.
